survey: A gold five-pointed sheriff star badge seen nearly front-on, turned slightly so its face tips a little toward the lower right. The face has a raised rim and bevelled ridges that run from the centre to each point. A small gold ball is fixed to the tip of each of the five points. Each ball is a sphere, so it reads correctly from any angle, and each sits where its point ends. In the centre, a round red gem sits in a gold bezel. The bezel is a near-circle that is very slightly elliptical, which fits a face tipped only a little. The rim's thickness shows along the right and lower edges, which agrees with that small turn. The arms are of uneven length, but they are consistent with the face being foreshortened from one camera. There is no ground plane; the badge floats over a burst of rays.
